posts.title: AI Speech Distortion
posts.html:
Hey everyone!

I'd really appreciate your help with something.

I'm struggling to generate videos where characters speak a language other than English.

I'm using Seedance 2 and keeping each video under 10 seconds, but it still distorts some of the words in the speech.

My native language is Armenian, and I'm trying to create videos in Armenian. I generate the exact audio using ElevenLabs, upload it as an audio reference, and provide a very detailed prompt explaining how the characters should speak and lip-sync. Unfortunately, the generated result still changes or distorts parts of the original speech.

Has anyone faced a similar issue? Is there a particular technique, workflow, or tool that can solve this?

I'd really appreciate any advice or recommendations. Thanks!

posts.title: How I Reached 500K+ Followers Across Social Media
posts.html:
Guys, many of you have been asking me in DMs how I achieved this small milestone.

Today, I would like to share the strategies and insights that helped me reach 500K+ followers across social platforms.

Currently, I am uploading content on five different platforms, and two of my accounts are monetized. Alhamdulillah, they are generating good earnings. (Along with content monetization, you can also generate additional income through branded content collaborations.) I would also like to sincerely thank @Daniel Riley , @Mateo Starcevic Filipovic , and @Graham Riley for their support and for building such an amazing community — one that not only teaches but also provides feedback and answers every kind of question to help people grow.

I am sharing my personal experience based on the knowledge I have gained so far. There are many experienced individuals here as well, so I would truly appreciate your feedback.

Here are some key points:

[ol:1][li]Choose a niche you genuinely care about. Your content should align with your interests and should not conflict with your profession or values.[li]Today, almost 70% of the technical work can be supported by AI. However, it still requires your creativity, daily effort, consistency, and strong time management.[li]Many people struggle to find a new niche. In today’s AI-driven era, discovering niche ideas is easier than ever. You can generate dozens — even hundreds — of niche ideas using AI tools. Additionally, while scrolling on social media, stay observant. If you discover a niche that interests you, explore it and present it in a unique way.[li]When it comes to short-form videos, the hook is the most critical element. If your hook is weak, there is a high chance your reel will fail. Ideally, your hook should be 2–3 seconds long. In my experience, anything beyond 5 seconds can significantly reduce performance — even if the rest of the video is strong.[li]Your hook should make viewers stop. It can be emotionally appealing, surprising, bold, or thought-provoking — but it should never feel ordinary or generic.[li]In short-form content, each clip should naturally lead to the next. Your video must be engaging, not just informational.[li]Video length matters significantly. For viral potential, 15–30 seconds is often ideal. Watch time and average retention send strong signals to the algorithm about whether your video should be pushed further.[li]Views alone do not make a video viral. Your content must provide value so people feel encouraged to save, share, and comment. These actions send powerful signals to the algorithm.[li]Focus on continuous improvement. In the beginning, everyone makes mistakes. Analyze your best-performing reels — understand what worked and recreate similar content in a fresh way, since your audience has already shown interest in that format.[li]Build a connection with your audience. Reply to comments — especially in the early stages. In my opinion, even up to 100K followers, creators should try to respond as much as possible. This builds loyalty and encourages viewers to return.[li]Many valuable content ideas come directly from comments. Never ignore them. Comments help you understand whether your content resonated with your audience.[li]There are four major platforms: YouTube, Facebook, TikTok, and Instagram. Distribute your content across all of them instead of relying on just one. Once any platform’s algorithm starts pushing your content to the right audience, growth can accelerate quickly.[li]In today’s AI era, video quality matters more than ever. Every scene should be engaging — not just the hook — to prevent viewers from skipping.[li]Your content should provide value. Even if it is entertainment-focused, it must offer something engaging, relatable, or meaningful.[li]Many creators make the mistake of deleting underperforming videos. This is not a good practice. Avoid deleting content simply because it did not perform well initially.[li]Do not repeatedly watch your own videos or constantly check analytics. Instead, focus on improving your content. Also, make sure your page settings are optimized — including your bio, professional mode, category, and about section — as these help signal your target audience to the algorithm.

Hey! I know it sounds a bit funny saying this in an AI community, but please don’t use AI to write your posts, replies or answers for you.

I realize that the advancements of AI now allow this, but we want to hear what you actually think. What have you been trying? What’s worked for you? Do you have some great advice? What are you stuck on? That’s the stuff that helps other people and gives us something worth talking about.

If someone asks a question, please don’t just put it into AI and copy the answer into the comments. Share what you know, and if you’re unsure about something, it’s absolutely fine to say so! We’re all learning here!

Your spelling doesn’t need to be perfect and you don’t need to write an AI essay. I’d much rather read a couple of sentences you’ve written yourself.

Good writing is good thinking. This is THE greatest AI community in the world, let's keep it that way!

And just to be clear, no rewards will be given for AI-written posts, replies or answers, or for activity generated by bots.

Get involved, ask questions and share your experience. Don’t feel you need to dress it all up before you hit post👍

posts.title: This is the level of realism you should be aiming for 🚀
posts.html:
I want everyone to really look at these different images of avatars for a second..

You can see pores, tiny freckles, micro hairs, uneven texture, light reflecting off real oil on the skin. Even the nose and forehead have that slightly shiny, imperfect look you only get from real daylight and real skin 🔥

Don't settle! This is the level of realism you should be aiming for in your prompts 👌

This is what separates AI art from “this looks like someone just took a photo on their phone at a cafe”. And that difference is everything if you want clients, brands, or social media to take your work seriously!

I've been seeing a lot of great work in here recently, and the quality of everyone's images is improving day by day!

We just need to be careful, because when something is too smooth and too perfect, people instantly clock it as fake. But like I said in the avatars module, when you have natural lighting, subtle shadows, skin texture, and tiny imperfections, it passes the subconscious test of realism

That’s why we focus so much in the course on things like lighting, lenses, skin detail

If you can get to this level, you’re not making pretty AI images anymore. You’re making content that can actually be used in ads, UGC, fashion shoots, and client work.

That’s the bar we’re aiming for inside AVB, let's do it! 😁🔥

posts.title: Creating Close up “Yapping” Videos 😆
posts.html:
Hey! Been spending some time trying these “yapping” ads, and it’s crazy how natural you can get them looking now 🤣

They do super well on socials and ads, because people love hearing people 'yap'.

These prompts are very handheld heavy, you want it to feel like someone has just picked up their phone and started chatting.

I’ve shared the prompts below. You can change the reference images, change the dialogue they say, location etc.

And if you give the prompts to your AI chat they will make any changes you want, while keeping the structure.

Definitely worth experimenting with!

Enjoy (Seedance 2.5 30seconds 1080p)

⭐ 𝐅𝐈𝐑𝐒𝐓 𝐕𝐈𝐃𝐄𝐎 𝐏𝐑𝐎𝐌𝐏𝐓:

Create a 30-second ultra-realistic vertical 9:16 front-facing smartphone selfie video using the provided reference image as the exact visual reference for the woman, her appearance, bedroom, bed, body position, lighting, camera distance and intimate close framing. The entire clip must feel like a completely real woman lying on her stomach in bed casually recording herself while rambling to her followers. This must NOT resemble a static AI talking-head video. The camera, her head, eyes, eyebrows, mouth, shoulders, hair and free hand must all remain naturally alive throughout the entire recording. The overall feeling is spontaneous, slightly messy, conversational TikTok footage rather than a planned advertisement.

ABSOLUTE CAMERA OWNERSHIP LOCK — CRITICAL

THE CAMERA ITSELF IS THE SMARTPHONE SHE IS HOLDING. The viewer is seeing the image directly FROM the front-facing camera of the phone in her hand. Therefore there is NO PHYSICAL SMARTPHONE VISIBLE ANYWHERE IN THE VIDEO. Do NOT generate a second phone. Do NOT put a phone in her visible hand. Do NOT show a phone lying on the bed. Do NOT show the edge, back, reflection or screen of the filming device. The phone exists ONLY as the camera viewpoint. One of her arms extends naturally toward the camera because that hand is physically holding the filming device, but the actual hand and phone remain outside the crop. Her OTHER hand is free and is the ONLY hand allowed to appear on screen. At absolutely no point may two hands be visible. At absolutely no point may any phone be visible. Treat this exactly like real front-camera footage: the device being used to record cannot appear inside its own image.

posts.title: 700,000+ followers across platforms
posts.html:
Over the past months I’ve been testing and scaling multiple social accounts, and at this point I’ve crossed 700,000+ followers across platforms (what you see here is just part of my TikTok accounts — Instagram not included).

At this point, I feel like I’ve built a solid blueprint to grow and monetize accounts without showing your face, mainly using AI content.

One thing most people get wrong:you don’t need a big account. On TikTok, you need one piece of content that hits.

Here’s the simple breakdown of what has consistently worked for me:

  1. Start correctly Don’t create a brand-new email just for TikTok. Use an email with some history — it helps with trust from day one.
  1. Pick a niche, If possible, go specific (even though broader niches can still work in some cases).For example: not “fitness” — but “home workouts for busy moms.”

Clarity wins

  1. “Train” the algorithm (5–10 days)Before posting anything, spend a few days shaping your feed around your niche. Watch only content related to your niche (e.g. dog training, relationships, motivation).

Then start interacting:like, save, and engage with similar content for a few more days.

Follow a few niche-relevant accounts. You’re basically telling TikTok: this is who I am and who I want to reach.

  1. Start posting (consistency > perfection)

[ul][li]1–2 posts per day for the first 10–15 days[li]Then scale to 3–5 posts/day if possible

Volume matters, especially at the beginning.

  1. Engage or you’re wasting trafficReply to comments. Stay active. Don’t just post and disappear.

Using this approach, it’s actually hard not to reach your first 1,000 followers.And from there, things start compounding.

Everything I do is organic and zero ad spend.And yes — most of the content is created with AI.

The opportunity right now is simple:attention → content → product → revenue

Curious to hear if anyone here is already testing something similar or trying to grow accounts with AI

Below is the VIDEO prompts, if you want to try it yourself!

All of these videos are made on Seedance 2.0. Because this is actual famous characters, 90% of the time Seedance will reject it if you add reference images, but you can try, sometimes they slip through (this will make it more accurate)

These prompts are really long, but its needed to get maximum clarity for these videos, they use the timestamp technique that is taught in the classroom.

⭐ 𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗠𝗣𝗧 𝟭:

posts.title: Ai Side-Gig: Fixing Real Estate Listing Photos
posts.html:
This is a great entry-level AI service for anyone here looking to practice + monetize their skills.

A lot of homeowners sell privately on:

Facebook Marketplace

Local buy/sell groups

For Sale By Owner (FSBO) sites

And their photos are often:

Poor lighting

Low resolution

Wrong aspect ratio

Not optimized for listings

(I literally took these photos off a real live listing)

You can offer a simple service:

Photo enhancement + resize for listing-ready quality

What I did here:

Enhanced lighting and color

Cleaned up the image

Upscaled to 4K-quality

Resized to 3:4 ratio (4000 × 6000 px) recommended

Kept everything realistic (no fake staging)

This makes listings look more professional without changing the home.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Prompt I used (photo enhancement): Nano Banana Pro 4K

Enhance this photo to true professional real estate photography quality, as if captured by an experienced photographer using a real camera and lens — not digitally enhanced or stylized.

Primary goal: Restore real photographic depth, dimensional separation, and optical realism while keeping the image believable and trustworthy.

Exposure & Light (camera-realistic)

Correct exposure naturally based on the existing light in the scene

Lift shadows selectively only where detail would realistically be visible

Preserve highlight roll-off (especially windows, sky, light fixtures)

Do not brighten everything evenly

Interior lights should glow softly, not overpower the scene

Windows should remain partially blown or reflective when appropriate — no HDR look

Depth & Dimension (critical)

Establish clear foreground / midground / background separation

Foreground elements feel tactile and slightly more defined

Main subject is the sharpest focal plane

Background naturally softens with distance through reduced contrast and clarity

Avoid uniform sharpness across the entire image

Color (restrained & natural)

I resize and enhance the photos hosts already have

Use AI prompts to turn each image into short motion clips (camera movement, depth, vibe)

Then piece everything together into a feature-style video

I deliver both landscape versions (for websites / landing pages) and portrait versions (for Reels, TikTok, etc). The idea is to help listings feel more alive and emotional.
